The capture records `layout.margin` (used top, right, bottom, left, in pixels)
for each direct child of a flex container with a nonzero margin, and for each
`::before`/`::after` box of a flex host. The planner adds it to the layer's
inset in its item (zero except for text) and passes the total through as
layout-child margins, which the model already placed; the host check verifies
them like any other position. Margins scale with a uniformly scaled ancestor,
as padding does.

`getComputedStyle` reports a used length, so an `auto` margin reads as the space
it absorbed. The specified keyword is recorded separately in `layout.marginAuto`,
and any auto side keeps the container fixed, even one that absorbed nothing,
because it would absorb space as soon as the board is resized:

- **Chrome and other engines with the typed computed style map.**
  `element.computedStyleMap()` returns the `auto` keyword for each side.
- **Firefox, and every `::before`/`::after` box.** Firefox has no typed map, and
  no engine exposes one for pseudo-elements. The capture scans the inline style
  and every style rule once (nested rules, `@media` and `@supports` that apply,
  `@layer`, `@import`ed and adopted sheets) for margins that could be `auto`:
  `auto` itself, or a value resolved later (`var()`, `env()`, `attr()`,
  `inherit`, `revert`). A pseudo-element rule is matched against its host.
  Logical sides are flagged on both ends of their axis, and `dialog` and
  `[popover]` elements count as auto because the user agent centers them.
  The scan ignores the cascade, so an overridden `auto` still flags its side;
  that only keeps a container fixed. When a stylesheet cannot be read, or a
  selector cannot be matched, the element records no margins, which also keeps
  its container fixed.

then converts (a trailing negative margin, for example, moves nothing); one
whose item was moved by it keeps fixed geometry with its own reason.

content.text:
Item margins are in on the `phase6-flex-item-margins` branch, with the Firefox fallback. Nothing is committed yet: per our usual flow, the live Penpot pass comes before the PR.

**What changed**
- **Capture:** each flex item now records the margins the browser applied, and which sides are `auto`. That covers normal elements and `::before`/`::after` boxes.
- **How `auto` is detected:**
  - **Chrome** reports `auto` directly through `computedStyleMap()`.
  - **Firefox, and pseudo-elements in any browser** have no such API. The fallback scans the page's stylesheets and inline styles for any rule that could make a side `auto` (including `var()`, `inherit` and `revert`), matching `::before`/`::after` rules against their host element. It errs on the side of flagging, which only keeps a container fixed. If a stylesheet can't be read, no margins are recorded for that element, which also keeps its container fixed.
- **Planner:** margins become Penpot layout-child margins. Any `auto` margin keeps the container fixed, since Penpot has no equivalent. A negative margin is treated as zero, and the container converts only if the browser's positions still match without it.

**Checks**
- **Real Firefox:** I ran the extractor in Playwright's Firefox 148 and Chromium. Both made the same decision for all 85 fixture containers (78 convert).
- **Real pages:** on the 6 pages that still capture, conversion goes from 56% to 69% (+140 containers, −1).
- **Suite:** 475 of 476 tests pass in the full run, along with typechecks, the production build and `check:dist`. The failure is the `fetch-html` rate-limit test in `api/fetch-html.test.ts`, which this change doesn't touch; it passed 3 of 3 times on its own, so it looks flaky under load.
- **Screenshots:** only the flex fixture's reference screenshots and scene changed. The baselines now record Chrome 156.

**Findings you should know about**
- **Margins weren't the main blocker.** October's estimate of about 307 margin-blocked containers lumped other causes in. Of the 164 containers that still don't match, none has a margin left. 118 are one MDN sidebar pattern: a `::before` chevron that imports as an unsupported fixed layer outside its row. Another 22 have plain text beside other elements. I re-ranked the follow-ups in `docs/importer-native-layout.md` and refreshed the plan's "Next batch".
- **5 of the 12 trial pages now time out:** vite.dev, Stripe, Linear, Tailwind and GitHub hit the 30-second analysis limit. A `main` build fails the same way, so the sites have changed; it isn't this change.
- **The Firefox check is a one-off script** in my scratch folder, not part of the suite, because the repo doesn't depend on Playwright.

Should I run the live Penpot pass through Orca now? It needs your Penpot tab open in the test file. After that I'd commit and open the PR.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head phase6-flex-item-margins --title "Pass flex item margins through to native layouts" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Top follow-up from the #55 real-page trial: flex item margins now become Penpot layout-child margins instead of keeping their containers fixed.

## Changes
- **Capture**: `layout.margin` (used px) and `layout.marginAuto` for direct children of flex containers and for `::before`/`::after` boxes of flex hosts. Scaled with uniform ancestor transforms; validated in the scene contract.
- **Auto detection**: `computedStyleMap()` where available (Chrome). **Firefox fallback** (and all pseudo-elements, which no engine exposes typed): a one-time scan of inline styles and style rules (nested rules, applying `@media`/`@supports`, `@layer`, imported and adopted sheets) for sides that could be `auto`, including `var()`, `env()`, `attr()`, `inherit`, and `revert`. It over-approximates, which only keeps containers fixed; an unreadable sheet records no margins.
- **Planner**: margins are added to a text item's glyph inset. Any auto side keeps the container fixed. Negative sides become zero, and the container converts only if the browser's positions still match.
- **Fixture**: four margin containers that convert (row, column, wrapping, `::before` icon) and two new kept-fixed cases (negative margin that moves an item, `::after` pushed by an auto margin). New references were generated with Chrome 156, and only `flex-layouts.html` changed.

## Evidence
- 476 tests; app/API/Worker typechecks, production build, `check:dist`. (`fetch-html` rate-limit test failed once under full-suite load; passes in isolation.)
- **Firefox 148** (Playwright, one-off): same margins and same decisions as Chrome for all 85 fixture containers.
- **Real pages** (6 of 12 still capture before the 30 s deadline, same on `main`): 580 to 719 of 1,036 flex containers convert (56% to 69%); +140 / -1.
- **Live, Penpot 2.19.0-RC5**: all three viewports import 78 native boards with no reverts, and margined layers sit within 1 px. The reflow probe matched 74 of 76 boards grown, all 76 restored (the two misses are the known compressed-wrap limit). One Undo / one Redo / a saved reload preserved 193 shapes, 78 layouts, and 14 margined children. The Bootstrap pricing scene converted all 8 planned containers; only header nav links moved, by font reflow with their 16 px margins kept.

## Findings, not fixed here
- Penpot 2.19 rejects `fontSize: 1`, which the importer gives visually hidden text (text fit scale 0.01). Every Bootstrap page fails to import until this is fixed; the live pass dropped those labels from its test scenes.
- The re-ranked follow-ups (offset generated boxes, per-side borders, stacking, anonymous text runs, grid) are in `docs/importer-native-layout.md`. Margins were not the main cause of the "do not match" bucket, despite the October estimate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

gh issue create --title "Penpot 2.19 rejects font size 1 on visually hidden text, failing Bootstrap imports" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Problem

On Penpot 2.19.0-RC5, importing any Bootstrap page fails with:

```
Unable to create Desktop layer "bd-theme-text" (text) from #bd-theme-text: [PENPOT PLUGIN] Value not valid: 1. Code: :fontSize
```

The whole board import aborts, so no layers are created for the page. This happens with native layouts both on and off. It was found during the live pass for #56, but that PR doesn't change this code.

## Cause

Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden` text (`#bd-theme-text`, labels inside icon-only buttons, and similar) is clipped to a 1×1 px box. The capture measures its glyph line at full width (for example 108 px for "Toggle theme"), so `textFitScaleOf` gives a fit scale of 0.01 (the minimum), and `textMaxWidth` is 0.1.

In `src/importer/penpot.ts`, `applyTextSizing` then sets:

- `fontSize = String(Math.max(1, 16 * 0.01))`, which is `"1"`. Penpot 2.19 rejects this value.
- `lineHeight = 1.1875 / 0.01`, which is about 119. That is also suspect.

The October trial imported Bootstrap pages on Penpot 2.18.4, so either the host's validation got stricter or the pages changed. I haven't checked Penpot's exact minimum font size.

## Scope

- In the 2026-11-03 trial scenes: 17 such labels on the Bootstrap cheatsheet and 1 on Bootstrap pricing. Every Bootstrap example page shares the theme toggle.
- Any page with `clip`/`clip-path` screen-reader text in a tiny box is likely affected.

## Possible fixes

- Don't import text whose element box is effectively invisible, such as the `.visually-hidden` pattern (1×1 px with clip), or import it hidden. It paints nothing in the browser.
- Or clamp the fitted font size to a minimum the host accepts, and keep `lineHeight` bounded.
- Either way, a failure on one layer shouldn't abort the whole board.

## Acceptance

- The Bootstrap pricing and cheatsheet scenes import on Penpot 2.19 without removing any layers by hand. The cheatsheet still has the separate `form-select` fill failure (#52).
- A regression test covers a visually hidden label with a fit scale of 0.01.

Found during the live pass for #56.
EOF

I opened issue #57: https://github.com/petercr/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/issues/57

- **What breaks:** on Penpot 2.19.0-RC5, the whole page import fails with `Value not valid: 1. Code: :fontSize`, so every Bootstrap page imports nothing.

Top follow-up from the #55 real-page trial: flex item margins now become Penpot layout-child margins instead of keeping their containers fixed.

## Changes
- **Capture**: `layout.margin` (used px) and `layout.marginAuto` for direct children of flex containers and for `::before`/`::after` boxes of flex hosts. Scaled with uniform ancestor transforms; validated in the scene contract.
- **Auto detection**: `computedStyleMap()` where available (Chrome). **Firefox fallback** (and all pseudo-elements, which no engine exposes typed): a one-time scan of inline styles and style rules (nested rules and nested declarations, applying `@media`/`@supports`, `@layer`, imported and adopted sheets) for sides that could be `auto`, including `var()`, `env()`, `attr()`, `inherit`, and `revert`. It over-approximates, which only keeps containers fixed; an unreadable sheet records no margins. Auto sides are read for every flex item, including one whose used margins are all zero.
- **Planner**: margins are added to a text item's glyph inset. Any auto side keeps the container fixed. Negative sides become zero, and the container converts only if the browser's positions still match.
- **Fixture**: four margin containers that convert (row, column, wrapping, `::before` icon) and two new kept-fixed cases (negative margin that moves an item, `::after` pushed by an auto margin). New references were generated with Chrome 156, and only `flex-layouts.html` changed.

## Evidence
- 476 tests; app/API/Worker typechecks, production build, `check:dist`. (`fetch-html` rate-limit test failed once under full-suite load; passes in isolation.)

- **Real pages** (9 of 12 captured in the final run; the rest exceed the 30 s deadline, same on `main`): 997 to 1,140 of 1,650 flex containers convert (60% to 69%); +168 / -25. The 25 had an `auto` margin that absorbed no space, which `main` converts but would not push when resized.
- **Live, Penpot 2.19.0-RC5**: all three viewports import 78 native boards with no reverts, and margined layers sit within 1 px. The reflow probe matched 74 of 76 boards grown, all 76 restored (the two misses are the known compressed-wrap limit). One Undo / one Redo / a saved reload preserved 193 shapes, 78 layouts, and 14 margined children. The Bootstrap pricing scene converted all 8 planned containers; only header nav links moved, by font reflow with their 16 px margins kept.

## Review fixes (Entire trail 393)
- Auto sides are now read for every flex item, including one whose used margins are all zero.
- The rule scan now applies `CSSNestedDeclarations` (declarations nested in a style rule's own `@media`/`@supports`) to the enclosing selector.

## Findings, not fixed here
- Penpot 2.19 rejects `fontSize: 1`, which the importer gives visually hidden text (text fit scale 0.01). Every Bootstrap page fails to import until this is fixed (#57); the live pass dropped those labels from its test scenes.

content.text:
I fixed both medium findings and pushed the fix to PR #56 (commit `df5ac2a`). Both findings are marked resolved on trail 393.

1. **Nested declarations were skipped.** Declarations nested inside a rule's own `@media` (for example in `.row::after { … }`) have no selector of their own, so the Firefox and pseudo-element scan missed them. They now count for the rule they sit in.
2. **Zero-width `auto` margins were dropped.** An item whose `auto` margin took up no space recorded nothing, so its container could convert and then fail to push the item when resized. `auto` sides are now read for every flex item. On the real pages this keeps 25 containers fixed that `main` converts wrongly.

While fixing these I found a bug of my own: the `::before`/`::after` pattern lost an escape in the generated script, and it's fixed in the same commit.

**Checks**
- Both cases have new tests.
- Firefox 148 and Chromium flag both cases identically on a test page, and the fixture decisions didn't change.
- All 476 tests pass, along with typechecks, the build and `check:dist`.
- The reference screenshots and scenes are unchanged; only `metadata.json` changed.

**Updated numbers.** I re-ran the real-page trial, and 9 of the 12 pages captured this time. Conversion goes from 60% to 69% (997 → 1,140 of 1,650 containers). The doc, the plan and the PR description now use these numbers.

The live Penpot pass still applies. The fixes only keep more containers fixed, and neither the fixture nor the Bootstrap pricing page decides differently.

The PR description was briefly empty: my first edit attempt didn't go through the `rtk` wrapper properly and blanked it. I rewrote it in full with the updates, so it's correct now.
